topic.title: The 2,000-Year-Old Computer Found in a Shipwreck

script.full_text: In 1901, sponge divers off a Greek island hauled a lump of corroded bronze up from an ancient wreck. It would take a full century to realize they had found a two-thousand-year-old computer. Hidden inside were dozens of interlocking bronze gears, cut with astonishing precision. It was a hand-cranked machine, built by ancient Greeks to model the motion of the heavens themselves. Turn its crank and it tracked the sun and moon, predicted their phases, even forecast eclipses years in advance. Nothing this intricate would appear again anywhere for over a thousand years. We assume our ancestors were simpler than us. But someone, twenty centuries ago, held the whole sky inside a box of gears. And then that knowledge vanished into the sea.
